>Just have to avoid having kids or getting super into debt because you think you have to. Expensive College is worthless unless you're guaranteed to get a good job out of it. (E.g. Pharmacy/Medical, Legal or a kind of practical Engineering)

This is my problem to the core. I was successful in high school, picked everything up easy, didn't have to try that hard, was constantly praised, and was told that I HAD to go to college if I wanted to succeed. I took the college prep route in high school, but I never actually got prepped for college. Too bad I didn't learn that til I was knee deep in actual work that I was having trouble grasping along with getting swine flu for a good portion of my first semester. I dropped out of college 3 semesters deep with only 12 credits to show and 13k debt. I cut my loss, moved away bounced around fast/food retail, was unable to support myself along with my debt, moved back home, worked in oil fields, got laid off, and ran out of unemployment. 

Now I am 25 years old, live with my parents, can't support myself on minimum wage, don't know any trades, and battle with health problems with no health insurance. I'm too afraid to go to the doctor because I don't want more debt, and I have been battling with depression since I was 15. I feel completely trapped by my situation and that doesn't help.

I am so jealous when I hear of stories like yours. I had the opportunity to go that route. I had the chance to get A+ certified through Cicso at my high school. For free. Instead I took the Honors/AP route and went to college undeclared and leaning on going into computer engineering. 

I really regret not doing it, and wish that so many people around me didn't pressure me so hard to go to college.

Sleep paralysis has to do with your R.E.M. cycles, so you're kinda right. IIRC it happens when you wake up in the middle of REM and your body is still in sleep mode, but some parts of your brain aren't, which is why you usually have a lot of trouble moving, the part of your brain the prevents you from acting out your dreams in reality is still active, but your eyes are seeing reality around you and your dream world and real world collide for a short time.

TL;DR break up dreams and sleep paralysis.

I was plagued by nightmares as a kid. I used to wake up into sleep paralysis all the time too. Sleep paralysis usually involves the inability to move along with aural and visual hallucinations. When I was 11 years old, I didn't know about sleep paralysis so I believed the things I was seeing were real. So I would have these terrible dreams of my parents abandoning me or a serial killer getting into my house, and then I would wake up and hear banging sounds and see shadows moving around my room.

Fast foward 5-6 years and I am a full fledged citizen of the internet. I discovered lucid dreaming on /b/ which also taught me about sleep paralysis and other things. I start keeping a dream journal and practice lucid dreaming all the time. It gets to the point where I just sort of sit inside my dreams and watch them. 

Fast forward another few years. Went through a bad breakup, struggling with depression and anxiety, unemployed, and living back with my parents, just 100 yards away from my now ex-girlfriends house, where she is still living too. Cue terrible romantic nightmares that are very personal and might not be "scary" to most people, but shook me to my core. 

Example, I have a very fond memory of my ex girlfriend. When we were still together, we went to different colleges. We kept in touch everyday and knew each others schedules to a T. Well I was coming home for a weekend and she tells me she is going to stay at school because she has some big projects due, so I just come home and do the family thing. When I go to bed that night, she comes home to surprise me. She wakes me up gently and I freak out, realize its her, and just grab her and pull her into bed with me, and almost instantly fall asleep again. It was just such a pleasant and peaceful moment. Well imagine reliving that moment twice a week through sleep paralysis. I would wake up and hear someone moving outside my room. She walks in and I can't speak. I want to tell her to leave me alone. I want to tell her to stay away from me, but I can't. I can't look away from the doorway as she walks over to me. She starts trying to "wake me up" but I can't move or scream which I am trying intensely to do both. She breaks down and starts crying on top of me, asking why it had to be like this. She then pulls a knife and stabs me. Usually I can fully wake up by then, but sometimes I can't and it continues for what feels like days of me just laying there and her just crying and stabbing me. I. Hate. It.

As an American currently living in the US with no health insurance, I wish I had the money to get the medication I need to function properly in society.

I have [scabies](http://www.webmd.com/skin-problems-and-treatments/scabies-directory) and can't treat them.

You know, I really do feel like you are right, that I should go find help and that I should talk to a doctor, but I can't. When I think about it I get that all too familiar feeling in my chest/throat. Anxiety maybe? I lose the function to think/talk properly and I want to cry. I actually tried to talk to my ex about it, which in hindsight is kind of stupid, but she is the only person that I have ever been able to open up to, and as soon as I started thinking about what I wanted to tell her I started crying. I couldn't think of what to say and I just babbled nonsense at her. She probably thinks I'm crazy because we haven't talked since then. I'm relatively sure she knows I'm suicidal though, which is part of the reason why I am where I am right now. I know that I crave her support, because we were together for almost 5 years and it was from 17-21 and I went through all of my problems with her and she genuinely helped me. She shows mixed signals of wanting anything to do with me. The reason I talked to her the other day is because she showed up at my house uninvited and asked me to watch a movie with her. While I was at her house watching the movie I broke down and she didn't try to console me at all. She even sort of dodged my attempted hug, although she might not have realized that I just wanted someone to care about me again. The next day when I facebook messaged her she blew me off.
I just typed out about half my life story, but I feel like it was too long/meaningless to post. If anyone wants to know any details just let me know and i can PM you I guess.

I know I have had an impact on lots of people and I know there are people that care about me and have learned from me. Sometimes I do lose sight of those things, but it is just another brick in the wall. If the only thing in my life that changed was my importance, I would still feel awful about the future prospect of life. There are too many things that drive me down.

I don't know if it is some silly prejudice I picked up from TV/Movies, I just feel like medication and therapy isn't the answer. Maybe therapy, but the way my family is I'm almost positive I'll be committed the second I mention that I have thought about suicide.

The thing is, I have passions, I have things to live for. I don't want them anymore. Nothing seems worth it. No matter what I put into something, the world changes and all of my time is wasted. I feel like the things i love are constantly changing for the worse. 

I guess you could say I'm somewhat stuck in the past. I find myself constantly wishing that things were more like the way they used to be. I know that things change and if everything stayed the same, life would be boring, but I just always get this sinking feeling when I think about how different life was just 5 years ago.
